XCII. Opera pietatis et misericordie sollercia peruigili per nonnullos Christi fideles non inmerito sine quouis more dispendio debentur imitari, docente beato Paulo apostolo bonum facientes non deficiamus tempore enim suo metemus non deficientes. Ergo dum tempus hahe- mus, operomur bonum ad omnes maxime autem ad domesticos fidei. Ob quod nos Petrus Jodocus Vlricus et Johannes fratres de Rosen berg ad vniuersorum noticiam tenore presencium volumus peruenire, quod attendentes naufragium labentis mundi statum et temporum fluxum inconstantem et incertum culmen diuinum vbilibet, prout ex- pedit augeri, cupientes de consensu et voluntate domine genitricis nostre domine Katherine de Rosenberg et de maturo fidelium nostro rum dilectorum conciliariorum, videlicet Buskonis de Bernharticz, Wernheri et Przibikonis fratrum de Porzessin, Nicolai de Podnawicz, Jesskonis de Czekow et Wlczkonis de Dobronicz concilio monaste 94 Hum in Altouado Cisterciensis ordinis, in quo rex celorum et dominus deuotissime colitur assidue et laudatur, quod nostre et nostrorum progenitorum fundacionis existit, necnon abbatem et conuentum ip- sius monasterii quam plurimum nobis dilectos modernos eorumque successores circa omnes et siugulas gratias, quibus excellentissimus dominus noster dominus Karolus serenissimus rex Romanorum et Boemie rex ipsum monasterium abbatem et conuentum eorumque ho mines possessions et bona quecumque a steure regalis solucione, que vulgariter berna dicitur, et ab vniuersis et singulis bernis steuris collectis imposicionibus precariis angariis preangariis peticionibus vngeltis hospitalitatibus susbsidiis et grauaminibus et oneribus qui- buscumque de liberalitate regia suis patentibus litteris pure propter deum intuitumque nostri obsequii ac in remedium anime domini geni- toris nostri felicis memorie domini Petri de Rosenberg absoluit exe- mit quittauit ac perpetuo libertauit. Promittimus firmiter et sincere per nos heredes et successores nostros grauaminibus impedimentis et postergacionibus quibuslibet remotis virtute presentium perpetue et inuiolabiliter conseruare, nee quidpiam contra huiusmodi donacio- nis gratias vilo vmquam tempore venire facere jure siue facto. In cuius rei testimonium sigilla nostra et predictorum fidelium nostrorum Busskonis de Bernharticz, Wernhardi et Przibicouis de Porzessin, Nicolai de Podnawitz, Jeskonis de Czekow et Wlczkonis de Dob rouitz duximus appendenda. Datum in Crumbnau anno domini mille simo trecentesimo quadragesimo octano die festi penthecostes. November. 0. �?0. — Wusk von Harach schafft unserer Frauen in dem Kloster zu Hohenfurt sein Gut zu Königschlag in der Schenkenfeidner Pfarre zur Abhaltung eines Jahrtages für sich und seine Vorfahren. Ich Wusk von Harach hern Dyetreichs svn vergich offenbar mit dem prief vnd tuenn auch chvnt allen den, dy den prief sehent oder lesen horent, dy nv lebent oder hernach chvmftig sint, daz ich mit wolbedachtem mvet zder zeyt, dp ichs wol getun mocht, mit rat vnd gvnst meiner pesten vrevnt vnd auch mit guetem willen meiner hausfrown Agnesen vnd aller meiner erben recht vnd redleich ge geschafft hab vnser vrown zv dem chloster gen Hohenfurt mein gut 95 gelegen in dem Chvnigslag in Schenchenvelder pharr genant in dem Pavmbgarten, da Hainrich zden zeyten auf gesezzen ist, vnd daz mein vreys aygen gewesen ist, vnd daz mir gedient hat zehen schil ling phenning gult, mit allen den rechten vnd nvczeu, vnd ichs ge habt hab, vnd ich mit alle dev vnd dar zv gehort, besuecht vnd vnhe- suecht, also mit beschaidenhait daz der conuent vnd dy sammvng des egenanten chlosters daz selb egenant gut in uvcz vnd ¡n gewer schul- len haben ze alle dem recht, vnd ichs gehabt hah. Vnd wenn daz ist, das got vber mich pevtt vnd daz ich nicht enpin, so schullen mir vnd allen mein vodern dy herren in dem egenanten chloster vnsern jartag alle jar jaerleich begen mit einer gewissen. Vnd darumb hab ich vorgenanter Wusk in daz vorgenant gut recht vnd redleichen aufge ben vnd richtig gemacht zder zeyt, do ichs do ichs (sic) wol getun mocht, also daz ich noch mein erben vns furbas dar nach nicht schullen stellen noch seczen noch chain chrieg dar nach nimmer mer gewinnen. Daz dem conuent vnd der sammvng dez egenannten chlo sters daz geschaefft vnd dy red also staet vnd vnuerchert beleih, dar über so gib ich vorgenanter Wusk von Harach in dysen offen prief fur mich vnd fur all mein erben wolbesigelten vnd bestaett mit mei nem anhungunden insigel, vnd zv einem zevg pezzer sicherhait mit meines lieben prueder insigel Dyetreich Penisch von Harach, vnd mit meines lieben ohem insigel Hainreichs von Lozperch fur allen chvmftigen chrieg. Der prief ist geben nach Christes geburd drev- zehen hvndert jar dar nach in dem aecht vnd virczkysten jar dez svntags an sand Andres tag. Drei kleine, an Pergamentstreifen hängende Siegel in weissem Wachs. — a) Ein Schild mit drei Pfauenfedern. — f S. Bvskonis . De . Harach. — b) Ein Schild mit demselben Zeichen. — f S . Dietrici . De . Harach . Vergleiche LXXII. b. — c) Ein Schild in zwei Felder getheilt; in dem untern derselben erhebt sich ein Kegel oder eine Pyramide. — -j- S . Hainrici . De . Loszperch.
entries.english:
1348, 15 June, Krumau. — The brothers Peter, Jodok, Ulrich, and Hans von Rosenberg bind themselves always to respect and inviolably preserve the tax exemption granted to the monastery of Hohenfurt by King Charles IV. 1348, 30 November, undated place. — Wusk von Harach bequeaths his estate to Our Lady at the monastery of Hohenfurt in order to establish an annual memorial for himself and his ancestors.

XCII. The diligent, unceasing works of piety and mercy rightly ought to be practiced without delay by certain faithful of Christ, as the blessed apostle Paul teaches: “Let us not grow weary in doing good, for in due season we shall reap, if we do not give up. So then, while we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to those who are of the household of faith.” Therefore, we, Peter, Jodok, Ulrich, and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg, wish by the tenor of these presents to make known to all that, mindful of the shipwreck of the passing world and the uncertain and unstable course of time, and wishing that the divine summit be increased everywhere as is fitting, with the consent and will of our mother, Lady Katharina von Rosenberg, and with the mature counsel of our beloved faithful counsellors, namely Busko von Bernharticz, Wernher and Przibikor, brothers von Porzessin, Nicolaus von Podnawicz, Jessko von Czekow, and Wlczko von Dobronicz, we desire to preserve perpetually and inviolably all and every one of the privileges by which our most excellent lord, Lord Charles, most serene King of the Romans and King of Bohemia, by his open letters, purely for the love of God, in consideration of our service and for the remedy of the soul of our father of blessed memory, Lord Peter von Rosenberg, generously released, exempted, acquitted, and forever freed from payment of the royal tax commonly called berna, and from every kind of berna, tax, levy, collection, imposition, forced service, extraordinary forced service, demand, Ungelt, hospitality, subsidy, burden, or charge, the monastery of Hohenfurt of the Cistercian order, where the King of Heaven and Lord is most devoutly and continually worshipped and praised, which is the foundation of us and our ancestors, as well as its abbot and convent, greatly beloved by us, their present members, and their successors, and all their people, possessions, and goods. We firmly and sincerely promise, for ourselves, our heirs, and successors, with every burden, hindrance, and delay removed, by virtue of these presents to preserve these privileges forever and inviolably, and never at any time, in law or in fact, to act against these grants and privileges. In witness thereof we have caused our seals and those of our aforesaid faithful counsellors, Busko von Bernharticz, Wernhard and Przibik von Porzessin, Nicolaus von Podnawitz, Jessko von Czekow, and Wlczko von Dobrowitz, to be attached. Given at Krumau in the year of the Lord 1348, on the feast of Pentecost. From a copy made by Abbot Stanislaus Preinfalk with the abbreviations and personal seals of the original. [No. XCIII.]

1348, 30 November, undated place. — Wusk von Harach bequeaths to Our Lady at the monastery of Hohenfurt his estate at Königschlag in the parish of Schenkenfelden, for the celebration of an annual memorial for himself and his ancestors.

I, Wusk von Harach, son of Lord Dietrich, openly acknowledge by this charter and make known to all who see, read, or hear it, now living or yet to come, that, with a considered mind, at a time when I could properly do so, with the advice and consent of my best friends, and also with the good will of my wife Agnes and all my heirs, I have lawfully and rightly bequeathed to Our Lady at the monastery at Hohenfurt my estate called Pavmgarten, situated at Königschlag in the parish of Schenkenfelden, where Heinrich currently resides, which was my freehold and yielded me ten shillings of pennies, with all the rights and uses that I have held, and with everything belonging to it, cultivated and uncultivated. The convent and community of the aforesaid monastery shall hold this estate in possession and ownership with every right that I held it with. When God takes me from this life and I am no more, the lords of that monastery shall celebrate an annual anniversary for me and all my forebears every year, with a vigil. For this purpose, I, the aforesaid Wusk, have lawfully and properly surrendered and transferred the aforesaid estate at a time when I could do so, so that neither I nor my heirs shall henceforth make any claim or raise any dispute over it. So that this bequest and agreement remain firm and unchanged for the convent and community of the said monastery, I, the aforesaid Wusk von Harach, issue this open charter for myself and all my heirs, duly sealed and confirmed with my attached seal, and, for testimony and greater security against any future dispute, with the seals of my dear brother Dietrich Penisch von Harach and my dear uncle Heinrich von Loszperch. The charter was given after Christ’s birth in the year 1348, on the Sunday of St Andrew’s Day. Three small seals in white wax hang from parchment strips: (a) a shield with three peacock feathers, “Seal of Busko von Harach”; (b) a shield with the same device, “Seal of Dietrich von Harach”; compare no. LXXII(b); (c) a shield divided into two fields, in the lower one a cone or pyramid, “Seal of Heinrich von Loszperch.”
